content: Precision-only consensus with two categorical outliers. Excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula, ironcalc and lattice all implement these statistical functions and agree on the result to roughly 15 significant figures; the >1 agreement class among them is pure IEEE-754 last-ULP noise (e.g. CORREL: 0.7745966692414833 vs ...834 vs ...835) plus reduced display precision in the ironcalc/lattice recordings. pycel does not implement any of these functions and returns #NAME? (missing-function). libreoffice records a blank cell for every case — this is a suite-wide recording/ingestion gap in the libreoffice lane, not genuine LibreOffice behavior (see the batch note on the libreoffice-blank artifact). Live-probed on hyperformula/ironcalc/formulas/pycel: all four match the recorded classes; pycel #NAME? confirmed for every function here.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures + live probe (hyperformula/ironcalc/formulas/pycel confirm classes; pycel #NAME? reproduced)

content: KURT (excess kurtosis) is implemented by excel, formulas, gsheets, ironcalc and lattice (agreeing to ~15 sig figs; the split among them is last-ULP float noise, e.g. -1.1999999999999984 vs -1.2000000000000004 vs -1.2). Two engines lack it: hyperformula returns #NAME? and pycel returns #NAME? (both missing-function — live-confirmed: KURT(A1:A5)=>#NAME? on hyperformula and pycel). libreoffice records blank (suite-wide recording gap). Note ironcalc DOES implement KURT (unlike the legacy-alias functions below), returning -1.2.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures + live probe (hyperformula & pycel #NAME? reproduced; ironcalc computes -1.2)

content: Legacy-vs-modern function-name coverage gap in ironcalc. These forks use the pre-2010 Excel names (COVAR, FTEST, TTEST, ZTEST). ironcalc implements only the modern dotted successors and returns #NAME? for the legacy aliases — live-confirmed: COVAR=>#NAME? while COVARIANCE.P=>1.4; FTEST=>#NAME? while F.TEST=>1; TTEST=>#NAME? while T.TEST works; ZTEST=>#NAME? while Z.TEST works. pycel also returns #NAME? (it implements none of these). Excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula and lattice all implement the legacy names and agree to float precision. libreoffice records blank (suite-wide recording gap). Portability takeaway for the wiki: prefer the modern names (COVARIANCE.P, F.TEST, T.TEST, Z.TEST) for ironcalc compatibility.

_meta.evidence: live probe: ironcalc errors on legacy names but computes the dotted successors (COVARIANCE.P/F.TEST/T.TEST/Z.TEST)

content: CONFIDENCE (the legacy normal-distribution confidence interval) shows two independent mechanisms in one fork. (1) ironcalc and pycel return #NAME? — ironcalc implements only the modern CONFIDENCE.NORM (live-confirmed: CONFIDENCE=>#NAME?, CONFIDENCE.NORM(0.05,1,100)=>0.195996398), pycel implements neither. (2) Among the engines that do compute it, gsheets diverges from the excel/formulas/hyperformula/lattice consensus at the ~8th significant figure (0.1959963986120195 vs 0.19599639845400538 for the 95% case; 0.9106931848827708 vs 0.9106931838592245 for the 99% case) — a genuine algorithmic difference in gsheets's inverse-normal (NORM.S.INV) approximation, not last-ULP noise. libreoffice records blank (suite-wide recording gap).

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures (gsheets normal-inverse divergence) + live probe (ironcalc CONFIDENCE #NAME? vs CONFIDENCE.NORM ok)

content: CONFIDENCE.T (Student-t confidence interval) is implemented everywhere except pycel (#NAME?, missing-function). Among the implementers, hyperformula produces a value that diverges from the consensus at the ~8th significant figure: 0.71049212538 vs the excel/formulas/gsheets consensus 0.7104921387393245 (medium-sample case), and 0.41277970947 vs 0.4127797123256051 (small-sample case). This is a genuine algorithmic difference in hyperformula's inverse-t (T.INV.2T) routine, not IEEE rounding — live-reproduced exactly (hyperformula CONFIDENCE.T(0.05,2.5,50)=>0.71049212538). ironcalc and lattice differ only in recorded display precision (0.710492139, 0.412779712). libreoffice records blank (suite-wide recording gap).

_meta.evidence: live probe reproduced hyperformula's divergent 0.71049212538 / 0.41277970947 (8th-sig-fig algorithmic difference in inverse-t)

content: FORECAST-family coverage matrix. excel, formulas, gsheets and lattice implement both the legacy FORECAST and the modern FORECAST.LINEAR and agree to float precision (5.8 vs 5.800000000000001). The gaps differ by engine: hyperformula and ironcalc implement NEITHER name (both #NAME?, live-confirmed); pycel is asymmetric — it implements the legacy FORECAST (returns 5.799999999999999) but NOT FORECAST.LINEAR (#NAME?), live-confirmed. So FORECAST/forecast-linear-fit has pycel in the numeric class while FORECAST.LINEAR/forecast-linear-canonical has pycel in the #NAME? class; that is the only structural difference between the two forks. libreoffice records blank (suite-wide recording gap). Wiki takeaway: FORECAST.LINEAR is less portable than the legacy FORECAST across the OSS engines.

_meta.evidence: live probe: hyperformula & ironcalc #NAME? for both names; pycel computes FORECAST (5.8) but #NAME? for FORECAST.LINEAR

content: INTERCEPT (y-intercept of the least-squares line) is implemented by excel, formulas, gsheets, ironcalc, lattice AND pycel (all agree to float precision, e.g. 2.2 vs 2.1999999999999997 vs 2.199999999999996). Only hyperformula lacks it, returning #NAME? (missing-function, live-confirmed: INTERCEPT(B1:B5,A1:A5)=>#NAME?). libreoffice records blank (suite-wide recording gap). Note the contrast with SLOPE, which hyperformula DOES implement — hyperformula's linear-regression coverage is incomplete (SLOPE yes, INTERCEPT/FORECAST no).

_meta.evidence: live probe: hyperformula INTERCEPT #NAME?, SLOPE ok; all other engines incl pycel compute INTERCEPT

content: SLOPE (slope of the least-squares line) is implemented by all seven live engines including pycel (excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula, ironcalc, lattice, pycel all in the numeric class), agreeing to float precision — 0.6 vs 0.6000000000000001 vs 0.6000000000000004. The only categorical outlier is libreoffice, which records a blank cell; this is the suite-wide libreoffice recording/ingestion gap, not genuine behavior. There is effectively no functional divergence here beyond last-ULP float noise and the libreoffice artifact.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures + live probe (all pure engines incl pycel compute SLOPE=0.7 on probe grid)

content: MARGINOFERROR is a genuine Google Sheets-native statistical function (documented at support.google.com/docs/answer/12487850) with no Excel equivalent. Per Google's docs it is defined as MARGINOFERROR(range, confidence) = CONFIDENCE.T(1 - confidence, STDEV(range), COUNT(range)). gsheets and lattice both implement it and agree to ~11 significant figures (0.04718417110127355 vs 0.047184171101276186; 0.09428439626864216 vs 0.0942843962686051), confirming lattice mirrors the Google semantics. excel, formulas, hyperformula, ironcalc and pycel all lack the function and return #NAME? (live-confirmed on all four pure engines). libreoffice records blank. Identity verified live: CONFIDENCE.T(0.95, STDEV(1..5), 5) = 0.047184171101 on hyperformula/formulas, matching the recorded gsheets/lattice values to ~13 sig figs. Note the corpus passes an unusually low 'confidence' arg (0.05 / 0.01), which is why the recorded margins are tiny; the wiki examples use 0.95 / 0.99.

_meta.evidence: wiki page documents the CONFIDENCE.T identity; live probe reproduces the gsheets/lattice value to 13 sig figs; all 4 pure engines #NAME?

content: DSTDEV (sample standard deviation over a database range with field + criteria) is implemented by excel, gsheets, ironcalc and lattice, which agree to float precision (1.4142135623730951 vs 1.414213562; 2.8284271247461903 vs 2.828427125). The three engines built on non-database-aware cores return #NAME?: formulas, hyperformula and pycel do not implement the D* database functions (live-confirmed: DSTDEV=>#NAME? on formulas/hyperformula/pycel). ironcalc DOES implement DSTDEV (a malformed probe grid returned #VALUE! from ironcalc, confirming the parser is present and only the field/criteria binding failed; the recorded corpus grid yields the correct number). libreoffice records blank (suite-wide recording gap). This matches the established DSUM story in DV-0011 (formulas/hyperformula/pycel lack the whole D* family).

_meta.evidence: live probe: formulas/hyperformula/pycel #NAME?; ironcalc parses DSTDEV (#VALUE! on malformed grid, number on corpus grid). Aligns with DV-0011.

content: HYPERLINK creates a clickable link, and the engines that implement it surface the DISPLAY TEXT as the cell's scalar value: with no label the url is shown, with a label the label is shown. gsheets and hyperformula both return the plain string ('https://example.com' for the url-only form, 'click me' for the labelled form) — live-confirmed on hyperformula. formulas, ironcalc and pycel do not implement HYPERLINK and return #NAME? (missing-function, live-confirmed). Notably excel, lattice and libreoffice are ABSENT from the recorded partition for both cases: their HYPERLINK results were not captured (likely skipped or recorded as an opaque rich-link value rather than a comparable scalar). Excel's HYPERLINK does return the label text as the cell value, so it would be expected to join the gsheets/hyperformula string class — this needs live Excel confirmation.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures + live probe (hyperformula returns the string; formulas/ironcalc/pycel #NAME?). Excel/lattice/libreoffice not in partition — unresolved.

content: TRUE() and FALSE() (the boolean literal functions) are computed identically by all seven live engines: excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula, ironcalc, lattice and pycel all return the boolean TRUE / FALSE (live-confirmed on all four pure engines). The ONLY divergent branch is libreoffice, which records a blank cell. Because no spreadsheet engine genuinely returns blank for =TRUE(), and because libreoffice records blank across the ENTIRE statistical-analytics, database and external suites (every single case in this batch), this is a systematic recording/ingestion gap in the libreoffice lane — the libreoffice fixtures for these suites were not populated with real results. It is a harness artifact, not LibreOffice behavior. Flagged for the libreoffice lane owner to re-record.

_meta.evidence: live probe: all 4 pure engines return the boolean; libreoffice-blank is suite-wide (incl =TRUE()), so it is a recording gap not real behavior
